title: Joshua 21:9–42
context: The full list of the forty-eight Levitical cities with their pasture lands, given out of every tribe on both sides of the Jordan, including the six cities of refuge. The list is kept as one unit and closes with the totals for each family.

verses.text: They gave out of the tribe of the children of Judah, and out of the tribe of the children of Simeon, these cities which are mentioned by name:
verses.arminianNotes: The list begins with cities from Judah and Simeon, named one by one. Arminian readers see attention to specific places as a sign that God’s promises were fulfilled in real, identifiable locations.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the detailed record as testimony to God’s faithfulness. Naming each city turns a general command into a documented reality that later generations could check.

verses.text: and they were for the children of Aaron, of the families of the Kohathites, who were of the children of Levi; for theirs was the first lot.
verses.arminianNotes: These cities go to Aaron’s descendants among the Kohathites, who received the first lot. Arminian readers see the priestly family honored with the first portion in keeping with their role in worship.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see God’s ordering of the priesthood reflected in the allotment. The note that theirs was the first lot underlines the priority of priestly service in Israel’s life.

verses.text: They gave them Kiriath Arba, named after the father of Anak (also called Hebron), in the hill country of Judah, with its pasture lands around it.
verses.arminianNotes: They receive Kiriath Arba, also called Hebron, with its pasture lands in Judah’s hill country. Arminian readers see a significant city given to the priests, placing worship at the heart of Judah’s territory.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise note the prominence of Hebron in Israel’s story. The verse explains the city’s older name, connecting the allotment with earlier narratives about the land and its former inhabitants.

verses.text: But they gave the fields of the city and its villages to Caleb the son of Jephunneh for his possession.
verses.arminianNotes: The fields and villages of Hebron go to Caleb as his possession. Arminian readers see Caleb’s earlier reward, recorded in Joshua 14, honored even while the city itself is given to the priests.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see God keeping faith with Caleb while providing for the Levites. The arrangement shows that one promise is not cancelled to fulfill another; both are carefully kept.

verses.text: To the children of Aaron the priest they gave Hebron with its pasture lands, the city of refuge for the man slayer, Libnah with its pasture lands,
verses.arminianNotes: Aaron’s descendants receive Hebron, a city of refuge, and Libnah. Arminian readers see priests living in a city of refuge, where justice and mercy for the accidental killer were administered.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the link with the cities of refuge described in Joshua 20 and Numbers 35. The placement of priests in such cities joins worship with the protection of life under God’s law.

verses.text: Jattir with its pasture lands, Eshtemoa with its pasture lands,
verses.arminianNotes: Jattir and Eshtemoa with their pasture lands are listed. Arminian readers see the list continuing city by city, each one a place where Levites would live among the people of Judah.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the steady record of God’s provision for his servants. The repetition of “with its pasture lands” shows that the Levites received land for their livestock as well as homes.

verses.text: Holon with its pasture lands, Debir with its pasture lands,
verses.arminianNotes: Holon and Debir are added with their pasture lands. Arminian readers see further evidence of thorough provision, so that the priestly families would have room to live and work.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the completeness of the allotment. Debir also appears earlier in Joshua, and its inclusion here shows conquered places now devoted to the service of God.

verses.text: Ain with its pasture lands, Juttah with its pasture lands, and Beth Shemesh with its pasture lands: nine cities out of those two tribes.
verses.arminianNotes: Ain, Juttah, and Beth Shemesh complete nine cities from Judah and Simeon. Arminian readers see a careful tally that confirms each tribe fulfilled its share of the obligation to the Levites.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the count matching the instructions. The phrase “nine cities out of those two tribes” summarizes the contribution of Judah and Simeon before the list turns to Benjamin.

verses.text: Out of the tribe of Benjamin, Gibeon with its pasture lands, Geba with its pasture lands,
verses.arminianNotes: From Benjamin come Gibeon and Geba with their pasture lands. Arminian readers note that Gibeon, whose people made a treaty with Israel in Joshua 9, now hosts priestly families.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see a city with a complicated history devoted to the service of God. The allotment shows God’s purposes moving forward through places that once stood outside Israel’s covenant life.

verses.text: Anathoth with its pasture lands, and Almon with its pasture lands: four cities.
verses.arminianNotes: Anathoth and Almon complete four cities from Benjamin. Arminian readers see the Benjamite contribution finished, with each place adding to the network of priestly settlements.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the careful record continuing. Anathoth is later named as the home of Jeremiah’s priestly family in Jeremiah 1:1, connecting this list with Israel’s later history.

verses.text: All the cities of the children of Aaron, the priests, were thirteen cities with their pasture lands.
verses.arminianNotes: Aaron’s descendants receive thirteen cities in all. Arminian readers see the total confirming that the promise of verse 4 was fulfilled exactly, with nothing withheld from the priests.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the precise sum as evidence of faithful obedience. The match between the earlier announcement and the final count reflects the chapter’s concern with exact fulfillment.

verses.text: The families of the children of Kohath, the Levites, even the rest of the children of Kohath, had the cities of their lot out of the tribe of Ephraim.
verses.arminianNotes: The rest of the Kohathites receive cities from Ephraim. Arminian readers see the non-priestly Kohathites provided for alongside the priests, each according to their role.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the whole Kohathite family cared for. The distinction between priests and other Levites is preserved even as both receive cities.

verses.text: They gave them Shechem with its pasture lands in the hill country of Ephraim, the city of refuge for the man slayer, and Gezer with its pasture lands,
verses.arminianNotes: They receive Shechem, a city of refuge in Ephraim’s hill country, and Gezer. Arminian readers see another city of refuge entrusted to the Levites, joining mercy and justice in their responsibilities.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the link between Levitical service and the cities of refuge. Shechem later becomes the setting of the covenant renewal in Joshua 24, which adds weight to its mention here.

verses.text: Kibzaim with its pasture lands, and Beth Horon with its pasture lands: four cities.
verses.arminianNotes: Kibzaim and Beth Horon complete four cities from Ephraim. Arminian readers see Ephraim fulfilling its share, so that Levites would live in the central highlands among the tribes.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see orderly provision continuing. The tally of four cities again shows the care taken to record each tribe’s contribution accurately.

verses.text: Out of the tribe of Dan, Elteke with its pasture lands, Gibbethon with its pasture lands,
verses.arminianNotes: From Dan come Elteke and Gibbethon with their pasture lands. Arminian readers see even a tribe whose territory proved difficult to hold contributing cities for God’s servants.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the allotment proceeding according to plan. The list records Dan’s portion without comment, keeping the focus on the fulfillment of God’s command.

verses.text: Aijalon with its pasture lands, Gath Rimmon with its pasture lands: four cities.
verses.arminianNotes: Aijalon and Gath Rimmon complete four cities from Dan. Arminian readers see another tribe finishing its share, reinforcing the picture of the whole nation supporting the Levites.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the careful accounting of each contribution. Aijalon also appears earlier in Joshua, and here it becomes a home for those who serve at God’s sanctuary.

verses.text: Out of the half-tribe of Manasseh, Taanach with its pasture lands, and Gath Rimmon with its pasture lands: two cities.
verses.arminianNotes: From half of Manasseh come Taanach and Gath Rimmon, two cities. Arminian readers see a smaller contribution suited to the half-tribe’s share, showing that the burden was distributed fairly.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see proportion in the allotment. The repetition of the name Gath Rimmon in consecutive verses is simply recorded as the edition prints it, without further explanation in the text.

verses.text: All the cities of the families of the rest of the children of Kohath were ten with their pasture lands.
verses.arminianNotes: The remaining Kohathites receive ten cities in all. Arminian readers see the total matching verse 5, confirming that the promised provision was delivered in full.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see exact fulfillment of the announced number. Each family summary in this chapter returns to the earlier totals, stressing faithfulness to God’s instructions.

verses.text: They gave to the children of Gershon, of the families of the Levites, out of the half-tribe of Manasseh Golan in Bashan with its pasture lands, the city of refuge for the man slayer, and Be Eshterah with its pasture lands: two cities.
verses.arminianNotes: The Gershonites receive Golan in Bashan, a city of refuge, and Be Eshterah from half of Manasseh. Arminian readers see a city of refuge placed east of the Jordan so that protection was available to all.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the cities of refuge spread across the land, as Joshua 20 describes. Golan’s inclusion shows the Levites serving the eastern tribes as well as the western ones.

verses.text: Out of the tribe of Issachar, Kishion with its pasture lands, Daberath with its pasture lands,
verses.arminianNotes: From Issachar come Kishion and Daberath with their pasture lands. Arminian readers see the Gershonites settled among the northern tribes, extending priestly presence throughout Israel.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the list moving tribe by tribe in orderly fashion. Each city named represents a household of Levites living among their fellow Israelites.

verses.text: Jarmuth with its pasture lands, En Gannim with its pasture lands: four cities.
verses.arminianNotes: Jarmuth and En Gannim complete four cities from Issachar. Arminian readers see Issachar fulfilling its share, so that Levites would be present among its people for teaching and service.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see God’s provision recorded precisely. The total of four cities again confirms that each tribe gave what was required.

verses.text: Out of the tribe of Asher, Mishal with its pasture lands, Abdon with its pasture lands,
verses.arminianNotes: From Asher come Mishal and Abdon with their pasture lands. Arminian readers see coastal and northern regions also hosting Levites, so no area lacked those devoted to God’s service.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the reach of the Levitical network across the land. The steady listing emphasizes the breadth of God’s provision for his servants.

verses.text: Helkath with its pasture lands, and Rehob with its pasture lands: four cities.
verses.arminianNotes: Helkath and Rehob complete four cities from Asher. Arminian readers see another tribal contribution finished, adding to the comprehensive picture of national support for the Levites.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see each tribe’s obedience documented. The count again matches the pattern of the chapter, in which totals are carefully confirmed.

verses.text: Out of the tribe of Naphtali, Kedesh in Galilee with its pasture lands, the city of refuge for the man slayer, Hammothdor with its pasture lands, and Kartan with its pasture lands: three cities.
verses.arminianNotes: From Naphtali come Kedesh in Galilee, a city of refuge, Hammothdor, and Kartan. Arminian readers see refuge and Levitical presence reaching the far north of the land.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see Kedesh listed among the cities of refuge in Joshua 20. The verse shows the northern tribes participating fully in the arrangements God commanded.

verses.text: All the cities of the Gershonites according to their families were thirteen cities with their pasture lands.
verses.arminianNotes: The Gershonites receive thirteen cities in all. Arminian readers see the total matching verse 6, so the Gershonite families received exactly what was promised.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see precise fulfillment. The repeated pattern of announcement and confirmed total highlights the reliability of God’s word and Israel’s obedience in this case.

verses.text: To the families of the children of Merari, the rest of the Levites, out of the tribe of Zebulun, Jokneam with its pasture lands, Kartah with its pasture lands,
verses.arminianNotes: The Merarites receive Jokneam and Kartah from Zebulun. Arminian readers see the last Levitical family beginning to receive its cities, completing provision for the whole tribe.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the final section of the list unfolding in order. The Merarites, described as the rest of the Levites, are not overlooked in the distribution.

verses.text: Dimnah with its pasture lands, and Nahalal with its pasture lands: four cities.
verses.arminianNotes: Dimnah and Nahalal complete four cities from Zebulun. Arminian readers see Zebulun fulfilling its share, so the Merarites have homes in the north before the list crosses the Jordan.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the tally confirmed once more. The count of four cities maintains the careful record that runs through the chapter.

verses.text: Out of the tribe of Reuben, Bezer with its pasture lands, Jahaz with its pasture lands,
verses.arminianNotes: From Reuben come Bezer and Jahaz with their pasture lands. Arminian readers see an eastern tribe contributing cities, keeping the Levites present among the people beyond the Jordan.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the eastern tribes included in God’s arrangement. This edition prints this verse without marking a variant, and it stands as part of the list.

verses.text: Kedemoth with its pasture lands, and Mephaath with its pasture lands: four cities.
verses.arminianNotes: Kedemoth and Mephaath complete four cities from Reuben. Arminian readers see Reuben fulfilling its share, binding the eastern tribes to the worship of the whole nation.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the tally completed for Reuben. Like verse 36, this verse appears in this edition without a marked variant, and the Merarite total in verse 40 includes these cities.

verses.text: Out of the tribe of Gad, Ramoth in Gilead with its pasture lands, the city of refuge for the man slayer, and Mahanaim with its pasture lands,
verses.arminianNotes: From Gad come Ramoth in Gilead, a city of refuge, and Mahanaim. Arminian readers see refuge provided east of the Jordan, so justice and mercy were accessible to every tribe.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see Ramoth in Gilead listed among the cities of refuge in Joshua 20. The verse continues the pattern of placing Levites in such cities throughout the land.

verses.text: Heshbon with its pasture lands, Jazer with its pasture lands: four cities in all.
verses.arminianNotes: Heshbon and Jazer complete four cities from Gad. Arminian readers see Gad finishing its contribution, so the Merarites are settled across the Jordan as well as in the west.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the careful completion of Gad’s portion. The phrase “four cities in all” closes the tribal list before the summary totals.

verses.text: All these were the cities of the children of Merari according to their families, even the rest of the families of the Levites. Their lot was twelve cities.
verses.arminianNotes: The Merarites receive twelve cities by lot. Arminian readers see the total matching verse 7, confirming that every Levitical family received its full share.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the lot’s outcome recorded precisely. With this summary, all three Levitical families have been accounted for exactly as announced.

verses.text: All the cities of the Levites among the possessions of the children of Israel were forty-eight cities with their pasture lands.
verses.arminianNotes: The Levites receive forty-eight cities in all among Israel’s possessions. Arminian readers see the grand total fulfilling the instruction recorded in Numbers 35:7, a sign of faithful obedience.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see God’s command carried out in full. The phrase “among the possessions of the children of Israel” shows the Levites living within every tribe rather than in a separate territory.

verses.text: Each of these cities included their pasture lands around them. It was this way with all these cities.
verses.arminianNotes: Each city includes its surrounding pasture lands. Arminian readers see practical provision for the Levites’ livelihood, so that their service would be supported in daily life.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see God’s care for the material needs of his servants. The closing note confirms that every city in the list was given on the same terms.
